# brickie

> brickie measures a Rust workspace (dependency edges between modules, complexity of every
> function) and checks the result against rules that the project's own maintainers wrote in
> `brickie.toml`. It has no built-in opinion about architecture: the rules are the project's
> architecture. This guide is for coding agents working in a repository that uses brickie. It is
> static; it does not read your project.

## Workflow

1. `brickie measure` reads the code (cargo metadata, rust-analyzer, tree-sitter) and writes
   `.brickie/cache.json` next to `brickie.toml`. It is slow, so run it once per round of edits.
2. `brickie check` reads the cache and the rules, prints diagnostics and exits non-zero when an
   error is not accepted. It is fast and never reads rust-analyzer.
3. Fix the code that each diagnostic points at.
4. Run `brickie measure` again (the cache describes the code as it was measured), then
   `brickie check` again. Repeat until the exit code is 0.

Rules of thumb:

- After any code change, re-measure before trusting `check`. A `stale/*` warning means the code
  changed since the last measure: run `brickie measure`. Config edits never need a re-measure.
- `brickie check --format json` prints `{summary, diagnostics}` for tooling. Use the text form
  to read, JSON to loop over findings (`id`, `code`, `level`, `brick_level`, `message`, `span`, `spans`,
  `rule`, `help`, `notes`).
- `brickie view` opens a local web viewer for humans (bricks, edges, findings, source). You do not
  need it.
- Commands accept `--config path/to/brickie.toml` (default `./brickie.toml`).

Exit codes of `brickie check`: 0 clean (or only warnings, or only accepted findings), 1 at least
one unaccepted `error` finding, 2 configuration, review file or cache problem (for example the
cache is missing: run `brickie measure`).

## Hard constraints

- Never edit the `[deps]`, `[[deps.rule]]` or `[[complexity]]` sections of `brickie.toml`, and
  never edit `brickie.review.toml`, to make `check` pass. These files are the project's decisions.
- Accepting a finding (an `[[accept]]` entry in `brickie.review.toml`, or Accept in the viewer) is
  a decision for a human reviewer. If a finding looks wrong or the rule seems too strict, stop and
  report it with the finding id instead of working around it.
- Do not split a function mechanically just to get under a complexity limit (tiny helpers that
  only forward arguments, one statement per function). Reduce the real complexity: early returns,
  a table instead of a chain of branches, a struct instead of many parameters, a clearer
  decomposition.
- Do not move code or add re-exports only to hide a dependency from the checker. The edge is
  measured where the code references the other module.

## Reading a diagnostic

```
error[deps/deny]: `engine` depends on `backends`
  --> src/engine/mixer.rs:42:17
   |
42 |         let io = backends::Alsa::open();
   |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ `backends::Alsa`
   = rule: deps.rule[0] "core must not use adapter" (brickie.toml:21)
   = help: depend on the port trait and receive the implementation from the assembly
   = note: modules: engine::mixer -> backends::alsa (uses, prod)
```

- Header: level (`error` fails CI, `warning` does not), the code in brackets, a message.
- `-->` is the primary location `file:line:col`; extra locations follow ("and N more").
- `rule` names the configured rule that fired and where it is in the config. Read it: it holds the
  reason the maintainers gave.
- `help` is the suggested fix; `note` adds context (for example the full cycle path).
- Every finding has a stable 8-hex `id` (in JSON, and in `brickie.review.toml` for accepted ones).
- The last line summarises: `error: 1 error, 3 warnings; 0 accepted`.

Vocabulary: a brick is a named group of crates or modules from `[[brick]]`. An edge is a
reference from a module in one brick to an item in a module of another brick. Edge kinds: `uses`
(call, type, constant), `implements` (`impl Trait for X` where the trait lives elsewhere),
`reexports` (a `use` with any `pub` visibility; private `use` leaves count as `uses`). Each
reference site yields exactly one kind. The edge target is always the module that DEFINES the item,
even when the code reached it through a re-export; a finding's note shows
`written <path as written at the site> -> defined in <module>`. Scope is `prod`, or `test` for `#[cfg(test)]`,
`tests/` and `benches/`. Edges inside one brick and edges touching a module that is in no brick
are ignored.

Nested bricks: a brick with `path = "<dir>"` is a composite; its children, rules and `exports`
are in `<dir>/brickie.toml`. Every finding has a `brick_level` in JSON (`root`, `root/web`): the
level of the tree it is reported at; its brick names are children of that level, and `rule` points
at the config file that owns the rule. An edge between two bricks is checked against the rules of
their lowest common ancestor (the edge from `web/ui` to `core` is checked as `web -> core` in the
root file). Test edges are checked like prod edges.

## Diagnostic codes and how to fix them

### deps/deny (error by default)

An edge matches a `[[deps.rule]]` with `action = "deny"`. Remove the dependency: depend on a
trait, type or function that lives in a brick you are allowed to use, and have the assembling
brick pass the concrete implementation in. If the code is test-only, use `#[cfg(test)]` or move it
under `tests/`, because many rules only apply to `prod`. If the dependency is truly intended,
that is a rule change for a human reviewer: report it, do not edit the rule.

### deps/default

An edge matches no rule and `deps.default = "deny"`. Same fix as `deps/deny`. The edge is
undeclared, so either it is a layering mistake (remove it) or the maintainers need to add an
`allow` rule (report it, do not add the rule yourself).

### deps/private

The edge reaches into a composite brick through a child that the composite does not list in its
`exports` (the message names the composite and the hidden child; `rule` is the composite's
config file). Use what the composite exports instead. Re-exporting the item through an exported
child does not help: the edge points at the module that defines the item. If the child is meant
to be visible, that is a decision for the maintainers of that file: report it (they may add it to
`exports`, or a scoped entry `{ brick = "x", scope = "test" }` for test code only).

### deps/cycle

Two or more bricks depend on each other (directly or through others); the note shows the cycle.
Break it: move the shared type into a trait or type owned by the lower brick, or invert one
dependency so that the lower brick receives what it needs from the higher one (parameter, trait
object, callback). Do not "fix" it by merging bricks in `brickie.toml`. Cycles are found per
level, among the children of one composite (`brick_level` says which).

### complexity/cognitive, complexity/cyclomatic, complexity/nesting, complexity/paths, complexity/params, complexity/lines

One finding per function and metric that is above the limit set by a `[[complexity]]` rule (the
limit is inclusive; "limit 15" fails at 16). The message gives the value and the limit; the label
says by how much it is over. Metrics:

- `cognitive`: how hard the function is to read. `+1 + nesting` per `if`, `match` (once, not per
  arm), `for`, `while`, `loop`, `let ... else`; `+1` per `else`; `+1` per sequence of like `&&` /
  `||`; `+1` per labeled `break`/`continue` and per direct recursive call. `?` is free. Fix: guard
  clauses and early `return`/`continue`, `?` instead of nested matches, extract a cohesive step.
- `cyclomatic`: `1 + if + loops + (match arms - 1) + let-else + && + || + ?`. Fix: replace long
  chains with a lookup table, data-driven code, or split by responsibility.
- `nesting`: deepest nesting of branches, loops and closures. Fix: invert conditions and return
  early, flatten with `let ... else`, extract the inner body when it is a meaningful unit.
- `paths` (NPath variant): the number of execution paths. Sequential decisions add, nested ones
  multiply. Fix: reduce independent branches in one function, separate unrelated decisions into
  functions with a clear contract, use tables for constant `match` arms.
- `params`: parameters other than `self`. Fix: group related parameters into a struct or options
  type that has a meaning in the domain (not a bag of unrelated values).
- `lines`: lines of the function. Fix: split along real responsibilities.

The rules of every level above a function apply to it (each level's rules select its own child on
the path); per metric the tightest limit wins, so a nested config can only tighten.

Findings in `test` scope are only checked when the rule's `scope` includes tests. Never raise a
limit; never add `#[cfg(test)]` or move code only to change its scope.

### stale/file (warning)

A `.rs` file was changed, added or deleted after `brickie measure` (the message says which).
Complexity and dependency data for it are old. Run `brickie measure`, then `brickie check`.

### bricks/unmapped (warning)

A module belongs to no brick, so none of its edges or functions are checked. This usually happens
after adding a file or module. Add the crate or module to the `members` of the `[[brick]]` it
belongs to, only when the right brick is obvious from the code around it; otherwise ask the
reviewer. No re-measure is needed: bricks are resolved from the configs on every `check`.

### config/missing, config/overlap, config/unassigned, config/member-outside-parent, config/unknown-export

Configuration errors (exit 2, printed on stderr with the code first; no findings are reported):

- `config/missing`: a brick has `path = "<dir>"` but `<dir>/brickie.toml` does not exist.
- `config/overlap`: a module matches two bricks of one file with equal specificity.
- `config/unassigned`: a module of a composite is in none of its children (children must
  partition the composite).
- `config/member-outside-parent`: a child's member matches a module outside its composite.
- `config/unknown-export`: `exports` names something that is not a brick of that file.

These are decisions about the brick structure: report them to the maintainers rather than editing
the config to silence them.

## brickie.toml reference

```toml
include = ["presets/layered.toml"]  # optional; paths relative to this file; merged first

exports = ["api", { brick = "internal", scope = "test" }]
                               # composite files only: children visible from outside (default
                               # none); a scoped entry counts for edges of that scope only

[[brick]]                      # group modules into a brick
name = "engine"                # unique in this file
members = ["my-engine", "my-app::api", "path:crates/engine/"]
                               # package name (all its targets), module id, or path:<dir>/
                               # (crates whose manifest is under the folder, relative to this
                               # file); the most specific member wins (path: < package < module,
                               # a longer path or module wins); a tie across bricks is an error
tags = ["core"]                # optional labels used by rule selectors

[[brick]]
name = "web"
path = "crates/web"            # composite: children in crates/web/brickie.toml (required);
                               # members default to ["path:crates/web/"]

[deps]
default = "allow"              # allow | deny: for edges that match no rule
cycles = "deny"                # allow | deny: cycles between bricks (prod edges)

[[deps.rule]]
from = "tag:app"               # selector: brick name | tag:<tag> | *
to = "tag:core"
kinds = ["uses", "implements"] # uses | implements | reexports; default all
scope = "prod"                 # prod (default) | test | all
action = "allow"              # allow | deny
reason = "app calls into core" # shown in findings
help = "optional fix hint"     # replaces the built-in hint

[[complexity]]
bricks = "tag:core"            # selector; default *
cognitive = 15                 # any of cognitive, cyclomatic, nesting, paths, params, lines
nesting = 3
paths = 200
params = 5
scope = "prod"                 # prod (default) | test | all
level = "error"                # error (fails check) | warn; default error
help = "optional fix hint"
```

Names, tags and rules are local to a file: a file's rules select only its own bricks. Each
`brickie.toml` (root or composite) has the same schema; `include` works in each.

Matching: for edges, the rule with the highest specificity wins (brick name 3, tag 2, `*` 1 on
each side, summed); on a tie deny wins. For complexity, per function and metric the most specific
rule that sets that metric applies (the lower limit on a tie). Unknown fields, unknown tags or
bricks and unknown kinds are configuration errors (exit 2).

`brickie.review.toml` (next to `brickie.toml`) lists findings a human accepted:

```toml
[[accept]]
id = "3fa9c1d2"                # finding id
reason = "why this is fine"
```

Accepted findings do not fail `check`. Do not create or edit this file yourself.
